why: This was the original substantial rotary-control candidate. The retained manufacturer bundle includes a STEP body, companion drawing, family PDF and mounting-hardware figures. It remains useful for instruments that prioritize a conventional capped control and panel clamping.
cautions: Its 15 mm shaft-length code is not the exposed height above a panel. The larger nut/washer can dominate spacing even with a small cap. The retained family rating distinguishes a 10 V DC limit from a higher AC rating; a ±12 V end-to-end connection is not acceptable.
history: Early baseline; later removed from the compact instrument, not rejected for all synth use.

why: The earlier AR design used this 50 kΩ linear slider as its mechanical reference. A 35 mm body was necessary for only 20 mm of travel; that discrepancy is the reusable layout lesson.
cautions: The 4 mm stem dimension along motion adds to the swept opening: 20 mm travel is not a 20 mm panel slot. Add tolerance, cap sweep and working clearance. The retained STEP belongs to the non-illuminated ALPS slider and must never stand in for a Bourns PTL illuminated slider.
history: Retained alternative after R12 replaced all faders with pots and separate stage LEDs.

why: This 10 kΩ green-LED ordering candidate was investigated for showing the active envelope stage in the moving fader stem. The PTL family provides separate LED connections; the stage indication need not follow the pot position.
cautions: The nominal body is 35 × 9 mm for 20 mm travel. The 10/15/19 mm lever options are actuator heights, not shorter slider travel. Green identity must not be presented as amber. Confirm LED polarity/current, all terminals, slot sweep, wash restrictions and factory soldering before adoption.
history: Research candidate; replaced for this instrument to reduce footprint, sourcing and assembly effort.

why: A familiar synth-shop family was retained alongside JLC/LCSC candidates because avoiding home soldering does not require avoiding ordinary synth controls.
cautions: The shop family label is not an exact manufacturer suffix. Shaft length, detent, taper, resistance, mounting height and PCB pin orientation must all be resolved. Do not copy a Bourns or ALPS footprint on the basis of a 9 mm family description.
history: Recovered from the R02 copy of the original v03 candidate register.

why: This family was considered during the SE1 compact-slider investigation. It is retained as a possible source of an LED-in-stem control for other instruments.
cautions: The family does not establish the exact fader inside SE1. Centre-detent, no-detent, resistance, LED color, body length and cap all need exact selection. A 20 mm travel listing alone does not prove a smaller body than PTL20.

why: The user recognized a compact slider on Weston SE1 and requested a replacement study. The official build/BOM resources are the correct identification route, rather than measuring a product photograph.
cautions: No exact BOM row or manufacturer identity was established in the conversation. This entry must remain an unresolved lead, not be silently relabeled as ALPS or Alpha.

why: This six-position alternative was considered when the octave selector’s footprint dominated the oscillator pitch. Its operating orientation would require an appropriately oriented interface board.
cautions: Do not compare only body widths. The shaft axis, terminal sweep, supports, connector access and panel bushing still need a full stack. It was not chosen as a drop-in replacement for SRBV160803.

why: A six-position selector outside the primary JLC route provides another option when mechanical compatibility is more important than a single distributor.
cautions: Its shaft/cap and pin pattern are not interchangeable with ALPS. Exact mounting and sourcing evidence remains a follow-up; do not import old price, lead-time or stock comments as a present guarantee.
history: R15 alternative; no new exact CAD acquired in this corpus.

why: This JLC catalogue candidate supplied the three-position function before the project preferred a matched T1 lever appearance.
cautions: T2 and T1 are different actuators even when the switching function matches. Lever geometry, movement and panel reach must not be copied from the selected T1 drawing.
history: Retained as a sourcing/actuator alternative; not the matched T1 baseline.

why: This six-terminal option was considered as an alternative procurement route for an ON–OFF–ON function.
cautions: DPDT means a second pole and a different body/pad arrangement. A positive stock listing would not justify silently placing it on an SPDT footprint. Verify the suffix and complete mechanical drawing.

why: The slide-switch candidate exposed a key preview error: the prototype’s authored rectangle had not been tied to an actual part or cutout.
cautions: Body size, visible tab, travel and PCB-to-panel reach are four separate dimensions. This part does not provide the three maintained states needed by MODE/SYNC. The user preferred toggle ergonomics for the instrument.

why: A common 0603 LED was the early inexpensive indicator proposal. It remains useful when the front-panel spacing allows a larger package than the later 0402 selection.
cautions: Color identity, brightness bin and hot current need exact evidence. White is not automatically warm white. A circle in the panel drawing does not establish an optical aperture or lightpipe, and the package must clear the adjacent jack/pot.

why: A common 0603 LED was the early inexpensive indicator proposal. It remains useful when the front-panel spacing allows a larger package than the later 0402 selection.
cautions: Color identity, brightness bin and hot current need exact evidence. White is not automatically warm white. A circle in the panel drawing does not establish an optical aperture or lightpipe, and the package must clear the adjacent jack/pot.

why: This exact Kingbright document was retained during compact-indicator comparison. Keeping it separate helps explain why the selected white part changed.
cautions: Do not transfer the chosen emitter’s current, brightness or height to this alternative. Use the exact datasheet and optical path. A shared 0402 label does not establish identical height or hot performance.

why: This smaller button was considered for a near-panel button PCB. It can be useful when a guided pressing surface decouples the fingertip target from the electrical-switch footprint.
cautions: Actuator height and panel/plunger tolerances must be selected as an assembly. The small electrical switch is not a finished performance button.

why: The retained AudioJacks STEP is a useful three-dimensional reference for a common synth-jack shape. Its original author and MIT notice are included.
cautions: It is community family geometry, marked untested in its source metadata. It must not be relabeled exact QingPu WQP518MA manufacturer CAD, and it proves neither terminal mapping nor dress-nut fit.

why: This connector was listed in the original control collection and in the related scope prototype. It is retained to distinguish a generic PCB audio jack from the panel-clamped patch-jack requirement.
cautions: Socket access direction, bushing/thread, switch contacts and footprint must be checked independently. A compact side-entry jack cannot replace a front-panel threaded jack simply because both accept a 3.5 mm plug.

why: The user chose black nuts for inputs and red nuts for outputs. These are mechanical parts of the jack assembly and a stable visual code, not merely a paint choice in the renderer.
cautions: The earlier 8.3 mm outside-diameter drawing was provisional. Confirm actual thread, nut thickness, engagement, seating and jack-lot compatibility. Leave room for the tightening tool and the cable plug barrel.

mpn: 15 mm aluminum cap, 6 mm bore listing
why: The user supplied a 15 mm aluminum-knob listing for the ALPS pot. It demonstrated why a visual cap choice should be recorded separately from the electrical control.
cautions: Nominal 6 mm bore does not resolve D-flat shape, insertion depth, retention/set screw, cap skirt or installed height. The listing was not a manufacturer mechanical drawing; no exact fit is asserted.

why: A low-cost 2.54 mm header candidate was considered for separately assembled interface boards.
cautions: Pin length, mating engagement, shroud/keying, plating and tolerances must match an exact socket. Pins should not carry knob torque or jack insertion force; provide mechanical supports.

why: This socket was investigated as a mating candidate, not declared a qualified pair with PZ254V.
cautions: An 8.5 mm insulator-height designation is not automatically the board-to-board spacing. Determine the combined seated stack, pin engagement and tolerance before drawing board planes.

why: This family illustrates a connector route with explicit mating and stack-height documentation, useful for evaluating separate boards at different mounting depths.
cautions: A family pair is not an exact order. Select pin count, contact length, tail, plating and orientation, then calculate the mounted separation and support geometry. No exact suffix is selected here.

cautions: A family pair is not an exact order. Select pin count, contact length, tail, plating and orientation, then calculate the mounted separation and support geometry. No exact suffix is selected here.

why: The source board-partition work retained a specific conductor document for internal harness planning. It is useful for replacing vague 'general pins/wire' assumptions with traceable material.
cautions: Wire resistance, insulation diameter, crimp compatibility, cut length and bundle routing all matter. Catalog material data do not qualify a completed crimp or establish equal current sharing among returns.
history: Later board-partition research, not an early panel choice.

why: This conductor was retained for the heavier board-to-board power/return proposal after the complete rail budget grew beyond the early preview allowance.
cautions: The termination, supported bend, hot resistance and actual routed current path must be verified together. A large wire cannot repair a narrow PCB return neck, and no soldering should remain after delivery.

cautions: Do not treat a catalogue maximum as an all-contacts-loaded installed rating. Verify mating face versus PCB numbering, wire/crimp range, per-contact temperature rise, cable drop, return faults and strain relief before replacing the abstract inlet boundary.

why: A retained TI document supports later supply/protection investigation. It is preserved as a research component, not promoted to a complete rail-protection circuit.
cautions: Controller plus MOSFET behavior must be checked for reverse current, missing rails, startup, shutdown and gate drive. A device that addresses one input fault does not automatically meet all three-rail synth power requirements.
identity_scope: family lead; exact package suffix unselected

why: This exact power MOSFET document was retained with the protection-controller study.
cautions: Use the gate-voltage-specific on-resistance, thermal path and safe-operating-area evidence rather than the name’s resistance shorthand. Fault energy and reverse conduction depend on the whole topology.

why: The inherited supply construction used this resettable-protection candidate. It remains useful as a case study in temperature-dependent current and voltage-drop limits.
cautions: Hold current is not a temperature-independent load budget, and a PTC is not an ideal current limiter. Source, wire, trace and component survival during the trip interval must be analyzed. Do not reuse an earlier low-current supply protection part blindly in the full instrument.

why: The exact manufacturer-specific TVS source was retained from the power project. It should stay distinct from another manufacturer’s same base marking.
cautions: Standoff, breakdown and clamp voltage are different specifications at different conditions. Check source impedance, pulse energy and leakage. A transient suppressor cannot establish safe sustained overvoltage on its own.

why: This manufacturer-specific SMAJ15A record came from the supply research and is retained with its own source document.
cautions: Do not combine ratings from different SMAJ15A manufacturers. The clamp waveform and thermal/current path must match the fault being claimed; read the polarity and pad orientation from the selected part.

why: The exact 1.2 kΩ resistor was investigated for stage-indicator current limiting after the compact emitter choice.
cautions: The retained one-page rating does not establish hot installed power capability at every ambient. Use worst-case rail, LED forward-voltage bounds and resistor tolerance, then the actual derating curve. No earlier ideal brightness demo proves this electrical limit.

why: The retained 2.2 kΩ identity is useful for tracing the original power circuit rather than substituting any generic resistor with the same value.
cautions: Check its role, dissipation and working voltage in the new circuit. A bleeder, LED limiter and signal resistor can have the same value but very different operating conditions.

why: This was the initial two-comparator proposal for trigger conditioning before the later source selected LM393BIDR.
cautions: Keep the exact version separate. Re-evaluate input common-mode limits, supply range, output pull-up and hysteresis rather than importing the B-version limits.

why: The initial brainstorming used TL074-class stages as a familiar starting point for mixing and shaping. Later explicit rail/current requirements drove more specific choices.
cautions: Select an exact suffix and package before comparing noise, input range, output swing and power. Do not use a generic family mention as a BOM line or equate TL074, TL074H and other derivatives.
